senses.definition: To see or view (someone, or something tangible) briefly and incompletely.
senses.example: Morning!—the Vestal Mother of the Sun / Seem'st thou to be, since from thy bosom born, / (Thou that first glimpsest—like a white-stoled nun!—) / He springeth forth—Oh! thou triumphal Morn!— / His race of glory and of joy to run; […]

senses.definition: To perceive (something intangible) briefly and incompletely.
senses.example: I have only begun to glimpse the magnitude of the problem.

senses.definition: Chiefly followed by at or upon: to look at briefly and incompletely; to glance.
senses.example: The door always opens directly into the kitchen, without any vestibule; and, glimpsing in, you see that a cottager's life must be the very plainest and homeliest that ever was lived by men and women.

senses.definition: To shine with a faint, unsteady light; to glimmer, to shimmer.
senses.example: O Lothſome place where I / Haue ſene and herd my dere / When in my hart her eye / Hath made her thought appere / By glimſing with ſuch grace / As fortune it ne would, / That laſten any ſpace, / Betwene vs lenger ſhould.

senses.definition: To appear or start to appear, especially faintly or unclearly; to dawn.
senses.example: Straitvvaies on heapes the thronging cloudes ariſe, / As though the heauen vvere angry vvith the night, / Deformed ſhadovves, glimpſing in his ſight / As darkenes, for it vvould more darkened be, / Through thoſe poore crannies forcde it ſelfe to ſee.

senses.definition: Sometimes followed by out: to provide a brief and incomplete look.
Chiefly followed by of: a brief and incomplete look.
senses.example: I only got a glimpse of the car, so I can tell you the colour but not the registration number.

senses.definition: A brief, sudden flash of light; a glimmer.
senses.example: [W]hat may this meane, / That thou, dead corſe, againe in compleate ſteele, / Reuiſſits thus the glimſes of the Moone, / Making night hideous, and vve fooles of nature, / So horridely to ſhake our diſpoſition, / VVith thoughts beyond the reaches of our ſoules?

senses.definition: A faint or imprecise idea; an inkling.
senses.example: Every surmise and vaticination of the mind is entitled to a certain respect, and we learn to prefer imperfect theories, and sentences, which contain glimpses of truth, to digested systems which have no one valuable suggestion.

senses.definition: A brief, unspecified amount of time; a moment.
senses.example: […] Alwin smiled, / When aught that from his young lips archly fell / The gloomy film from Harold's eye beguiled; / And pleased for a glimpse appeared the woeful Childe.

senses.definition: A faint (and often temporary) appearance; a tinge.
senses.example: Reuiued with a glimſe of grace old ſorowes to let fal, / The hidden ſtraines I know and ſecret ſnares of loue: / How ſoone a loke wil print a thought, that neuer may remoue.
